title: Document-grounding contract — fixture and report documents
description: The closed tagged union `benchmark/grounding.ts` reads and writes: the Tangle-authored fixture (the analytic oracle — sources, versions, elements, chunks, questions, material claims with closed matching predicates, the scripted per-question supply trace, scripted predicted answers, and the six separately-held RFC 9110 questions) and the keyless grounding report (registration, source manifest, the scorer's oracle gate, one scored scenario per scripted answer with its complete evidence trace and one terminal outcome per visible citation, reconciled counts, and a decision that cannot claim product adoption from a keyless run). TypeScript is generated from this document by `@jarenjs/emit`; the arithmetic an honest report depends on binds here through `$query` at validation time. Every object closes its properties, so key material or an undeclared member cannot be carried.

citationOutcome.description: The one ordered terminal outcome of a visible citation, walked in exactly this order against the attempt trace: unknown address first, then supply, then version status, then cutoff eligibility, then oracle support. A citation may not skip a state and may not carry two outcomes.

predicates.description: Closed matching data, never executable text: each required group is satisfied when at least one of its members occurs inside the space-padded officially-normalized claim text, and no forbidden member may occur. Authored with the fixture, before any result exists.

answerValue.description: The one answer contract of both the scripted and live paths. There is no free-prose member a material claim can hide in: the visible answer is rendered from the claim texts in array order, or from the abstention reason.

fixtureTrace.description: The scripted per-question supply for the keyless tier: which chunk addresses were retrieved and which were serialized as evidence. A member that could not arise on the shipped path (a superseded chunk in `supplied`) is a deliberate forged-reference proof the scorer must refuse, never a claim about the product.

census.description: The registered corpus size — fixed by the campaign's design, so a fixture that grew or shrank cannot validate.

rfc9110.description: The optional web diagnostic's six fixed questions: reference answers and the directly curated URL, and never a captured third-party body. They enter no fixture question or claim denominator.

citationRecord.description: One visible citation occurrence, claim-scoped, in reply order. Raw: duplicates remain here and are deduplicated only for set metrics.

claimScore.description: One-to-one predicate assignment and the supported-material-claim counts. A matched claim without a supporting terminal citation is one FP and one FN, never half credit. `f1` is null on a non-answerable question: it has no claim denominator.

oracleGate.description: The scorer's own proof, computed over the oracle scenarios before any comparison may print: exact ceilings, or the run exits without a table.

registration.description: Fixed before a score is read and hashed into `registrationId`: the fixture identity, the cutoff, the question and claim registers, the scorer's settled rules and the answer contract's revision. No observed result, clock, cost or key enters it.

matching.const: expected claims in manifest order take the earliest unmatched predicted claim satisfying the fixture predicates; one-to-one; no similarity threshold

liveStatus.description: What happened to one question in one row. `analytic` belongs only to the no-generation row; a failure stays in the attempt and makes the paired comparison ineligible.

liveTrace.description: The exact retrieval/supply trace of one question through the current path: ranked candidates, raw serialized blocks with duplicate neighbour expansion retained, unique supplied chunks, and the prompt bytes they cost.

liveQuestionResult.description: One question in one row, raw: the answer value, every visible citation with its terminal outcome, the claim assignment and the per-question cost stay in the report so every claim and citation outcome is auditable.

liveRow.description: One of the three registered rows. `documents-retrieved` never generates: it is the retrieval/supply ceiling, its results are `analytic` and its config-identity row is `not-run`. The two generated rows share every control and are comparable only on complete identical question sets.

questionSet.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the row's sorted successfully-answered question ids — what eligibility compares instead of walking two lists.

liveComparison.description: One paired treatment/control comparison over identical complete question sets: the seeded 10,000-resample paired bootstrap interval by nearest-rank quantiles, the one-sided lower bound, and the power that turns a null into a bounded null.

liveStratum.description: One corpus stratum with its own denominators. The fixture and LoCoMo strata are never pooled: no metric helper accepts rows from both, and only the fixture stratum carries material-claim scores.

livePlan.description: The frozen dry plan: everything the operator authorizes, credential-free. `planId` is the canonical SHA-256 of the plan's registered members; only a matching explicit authorization executes.

configIdentities.description: The shared config-identity envelope: generated rows reference the one resolved run identity; the no-generation row is `not-run` analysis.

registration.description: The keyless registration plus the frozen treatment: the exact current chunker/retrieval defaults, the shared prompt revision, the repair ceiling, concurrency and seed. Every value is effective, never a name.

matching.const: expected claims in manifest order take the earliest unmatched predicted claim satisfying the fixture predicates; one-to-one; no similarity threshold

groundingHandoff.title: Flat-baseline handoff
groundingHandoff.description: The committed downstream handoff: the flat-baseline query document executed verbatim over the validated live and web reports. Clock-free and byte-reproducible; every identity here resolves to exactly one object in its source report, which the query test pins.

liveDecision.description: The mechanical product decision over a validated live attempt. `adopt-claim-citations` is legal only when the document's own rows recompute every registered clause — the `$query` on the live branch refuses a forged adoption — and a missing or ineligible row can never be read as a pass.

captureManifestRow.description: One captured HTTP exchange as a report may carry it: url, status, byte hash and sizes — never a third-party body.

webSelection.description: One query's complete selection record: result order kept, at most the first three distinct normalized HTTP(S) URLs selected, every refusal named. Snippets appear only as counts — never as evidence.

webRow.description: One of the two web answer rows, over the same six questions, model, answer schema and budgets. No material-claim score exists on the open web: `claims` is structurally absent and support cannot be proven, only resolution.

ingest.description: The acquisition funnel of this row's corpus: every URL attempted with its outcome.

baseline.description: The flat baseline this diagnostic is registered against — linked by identity, never merged into its denominator.

policy.const: the first distinct normalized HTTP(S) URLs in SearxNG result order after existing URL policy; no learned selector, no authority boost; snippets are never evidence

decision.description: The product decision surface. A keyless report can never claim adoption: its state is `not-evaluated` by contract, and only a validated eligible paired live result may ever move it.

configIdentities.description: The shared config-identity envelope. Every keyless scenario is a not-run analytic row: nothing here ran a provider stack.
